eye_color.narrative: Based on 6 of 6 IrisPlex marker SNPs present on your chip, there is moderate agreement toward blue. The single strongest marker, rs12913832 (GG), points blue, and this locus alone drives most of IrisPlex's real-world predictive accuracy. Genotype and direction of effect for each marker is listed below.

markers.note: Single strongest known predictor of blue vs brown eye color. GG is associated with blue; AA with brown; AG intermediate. Accounts for the majority of IrisPlex's predictive power on its own.
Minor contributor; T allele associated with lighter eye color.
Modulates iris and hair pigmentation; G allele leans lighter.
Primarily a skin/hair pigmentation gene; C allele leans lighter across all three traits in IrisPlex/HIrisPlex panels.
Affects tyrosinase activity / melanin synthesis; A allele leans lighter.
Modulates overall pigmentation intensity; T allele leans lighter.

eye_color.method_note: IrisPlex 6-SNP panel (Walsh et al. 2011). Directional concordance shown; full published regression model not implemented — no fabricated confidence score.

skin_tone.uv_label: Moderate UV sensitivity — burns before tanning
skin_tone.narrative: Medium (Type III). SLC24A5 AA is the dominant signal — this locus alone explains the majority of pigmentation difference between European and African populations and strongly predicts lighter skin. However, SLC45A2 GG (ancestral allele) partially counteracts this, suggesting a light-to-medium result rather than very fair. TYR CA reduces melanin output further, adding freckling tendency and UV sensitivity. Combined picture: skin that tans moderately but burns more readily than average. Moderate UV sensitivity — burns before tanning. 6 SNPs combined.

height.narrative: Strong above-average height signal. GWAS PGS +401.1 from 29 elevated loci. Height is ~80% heritable in well-nourished populations. The GWAS polygenic score of +401 is the second highest in your profile, consistently pointing toward above-average stature. Realised height depends substantially on childhood nutrition and health. 3 curated SNPs combined.
supporting: rs1042725 (HMGA2): TT — HMGA2 TT — taller-associated allele, ~0.4 cm per T allele
rs143384 (GDF5): AG — GDF5 secondary variant — bone and cartilage development

intelligence.narrative: Warrior cognitive profile (COMT Val/Val). GWAS PGS +1064.5 from 8 elevated loci. COMT GG (Val/Val) — Warrior profile: higher dopamine breakdown in PFC, better executive function under load and stress.BDNF CT heterozygous — partial reduction in activity-dependent BDNF; sleep and aerobic exercise are particularly important for memory consolidation. Intelligence GWAS PGS is the highest in your profile at +1064, though this includes educational attainment and Alzheimer pleiotropic signals. 2 curated SNPs combined.
supporting: rs4680 (COMT): GG — COMT Met allele — higher prefrontal dopamine; better baseline performance but stress vulnerable
rs6265 (BDNF): CT — BDNF Val66Met T — reduced activity-dependent BDNF; affects memory consolidation and stress resilience

mthfr.narrative: Moderate folate metabolism signal. You carry both MTHFR C677T (GA heterozygous) and MTHFR A1298C (GT heterozygous) — compound heterozygosity that reduces MTHFR enzyme activity by approximately 50-60%. This impairs conversion of dietary folate to active 5-methylTHF and slows homocysteine clearance. Practical action: supplement with methylfolate (5-MTHF) rather than folic acid, and methylcobalamin rather than cyanocobalamin. Test homocysteine, folate, and B12 blood levels to confirm metabolic status. 5 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs1801133 (MTHFR): AG — MTHFR C677T — reduces MTHFR enzyme activity ~35% (het) / ~70% (hom); impairs folate conversion and homocysteine clearance
rs1801131 (MTHFR): GT — MTHFR A1298C — regulatory domain variant; combined with C677T (compound het) reduces activity ~50-60%
rs2236225 (MTHFD1): AG — MTHFD1 — feeds into folate one-carbon cycle; AG adds modest strain
rs1805087 (MTR): AA — MTR A2756G — methionine synthase; AA is wild-type (no impairment)
rs1801394 (MTRR): GG — MTRR A66G — B12 recycling enzyme; GG is wild-type (no impairment)

t2d.narrative: Elevated T2D risk. GWAS polygenic score is +116.8 (above average across 26 elevated loci). Note: rs1631619 GG (OR 5.0) is a population-specific finding from a Korean cohort and may inflate the PGS for non-Korean ancestries. Genotype pattern: 4 loci homozygous risk, 7 heterozygous (one risk copy). Heterozygosity at TCF7L2, KCNJ11, FTO and others indicates moderate rather than severe genetic loading — you carry one risk copy at most major loci, not two. Important: T2D is 40–70% heritable but lifestyle factors (weight, diet, exercise) interact strongly — genetic risk is not destiny. 12 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs7903146 (TCF7L2): CT — TCF7L2 T allele — strongest common T2D variant; impairs beta-cell function via Wnt signalling. TC = one risk copy (OR ~1.4).
rs1801282 (PPARG): CC — PPARG Pro12 (C allele) — absence of the protective Ala12 variant. CC = no protection from this locus.
rs5219 (KCNJ11): CT — KCNJ11 E23K T allele — affects ATP-sensitive potassium channel in beta cells; impairs insulin secretion. CT = one risk copy.
rs13266634 (SLC30A8): CT — SLC30A8 C allele — zinc transporter variant affecting beta-cell insulin processing. TC = one risk copy.
rs10811661 (CDKN2A/B): CT — CDKN2A/B T allele — affects beta-cell proliferation and mass. CT = one risk copy.
rs1111875 (HHEX): CT — HHEX/IDE C allele — affects insulin secretion pathway. TC = one risk copy.
rs4402960 (IGF2BP2): GT — IGF2BP2 T allele — RNA-binding protein affecting insulin signalling. GT = one risk copy.
rs8050136 (FTO): AC — FTO A allele — obesity/energy balance gene, indirect T2D risk via BMI pathway. CA = one risk copy.
rs76895963 (CCND2-AS1): TT — CCND2-AS1 T allele — TT homozygous in your data; OR 2.84 for T2D in published GWAS. Strong signal.
rs1631619 (LINC02630): GG — LINC02630 G allele — GG homozygous; OR 5.0 in Korean cohort GWAS. Note: high OR may reflect population-specific effect.
rs10741243 (TCERG1L): GG — TCERG1L G allele — GG homozygous; OR 1.75, 95% CI [1.38–2.23]. Intron variant with replicated T2D association.

alzheimer.narrative: Average Alzheimer risk. APOE status: ε2/ε2 or ε2/ε3 — very low Alzheimer risk (rs429358 not on chip). GWAS: 50 elevated loci, PGS +171.6. APOE genotype is by far the strongest genetic factor — it alone accounts for ~50% of genetic Alzheimer risk. Other loci (CLU, BIN1, CR1, PICALM) each contribute modestly. Lifestyle factors (cardiovascular health, cognitive engagement, sleep) meaningfully modify genetic risk. 6 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs9331888 (CLU): CC — CLU secondary variant — modest Alzheimer's risk association.

cad.narrative: Elevated CAD risk. GWAS: 25 elevated loci, PGS +111.0. The 9p21 locus (CDKN2B-AS1) is the strongest common CAD variant — it acts independently of LDL. Standard cardiovascular risk factors (blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, LDL) interact multiplicatively with genetic risk. Statins and lifestyle modification are effective regardless of genotype. 7 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs4977574 (CDKN2B-AS1): AG — 9p21 locus — strongest replicated CAD SNP; G allele OR ~1.3.
rs1333049 (CDKN2B-AS1): CG — 9p21 secondary variant — additive with rs4977574.
rs646776 (CELSR2): TT — CELSR2/SORT1 — LDL pathway, raises CAD risk.
rs1122608 (LDLR): GG — LDLR region — LDL receptor pathway.
rs264 (LPL): GG — PROTECTIVE: LPL G allele — lipoprotein lipase, higher activity, protective.

bmi.narrative: Moderate genetic BMI tendency. GWAS: 48 elevated loci, PGS +492.4. FTO and MC4R are the strongest common BMI loci. Importantly, BMI genetic effects are highly modifiable by physical activity — FTO risk allele carriers who exercise regularly show substantially attenuated obesity risk (Kilpeläinen et al. 2011). Genetic BMI tendency is not fixed destiny. 7 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs9939609 (FTO): AT — FTO A allele — strongest common obesity SNP; each A adds ~0.4 kg/m².
rs17817449 (FTO): GT — FTO secondary variant — additive obesity risk.
rs2815752 (NEGR1): AG — PROTECTIVE: NEGR1 A allele — neuronal growth regulator; protective for BMI.
rs10938397 (GNPDA2): AG — GNPDA2 G allele — modest BMI increase association.

triglycerides.narrative: Moderate triglyceride tendency. GWAS: 57 elevated loci, PGS +113.8. APOA5 and LPL are the dominant loci. Dietary carbohydrate and alcohol intake interact strongly with genetic triglyceride risk — omega-3 supplementation and low-carbohydrate diets are particularly effective in carriers of APOA5 risk alleles. 6 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs662799 (APOA5): AG — APOA5 G allele — major triglyceride-raising variant; OR ~1.8 per allele.
rs328 (LPL): CC — PROTECTIVE: LPL S447X C allele — gain-of-function, substantially lowers triglycerides.
rs2266788 (APOC3): AG — APOC3 promoter variant — increased APOC3 expression.
rs10830963 (MTNR1B): CG — MTNR1B G allele — melatonin receptor; affects fasting triglycerides.

depression.narrative: Elevated depression genetic signal. GWAS: 32 elevated loci, PGS +71.8. Depression heritability is ~35–40%; most genetic variance is polygenic with very small individual effects. BDNF Val66Met and COMT Val158Met are the best-studied candidates — but effect sizes are modest and gene-environment interaction (stress, trauma, social support) dominates. Genetic risk for depression is not predictive at the individual level. 6 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs1545843 (NEGR1): AG — NEGR1 — neuronal growth; first replicated MDD GWAS hit.
rs10514299 (TMEM161B): TT — TMEM161B — neuronal function; MDD association.
rs6265 (BDNF): CT — BDNF Val66Met T allele — reduced BDNF secretion; associated with depression vulnerability and stress response.

longevity.narrative: Moderate longevity signals. GWAS: 18 longevity loci, PGS +62.4. APOE and FOXO3 are the two most replicated longevity loci. FOXO3 G allele (if present) is associated with exceptional longevity across Japanese, American, Danish and other cohorts — it's the most robust non-APOE longevity signal known. CETP variants that raise HDL are also overrepresented in centenarians. Lifestyle (exercise, diet, sleep, not smoking) remains the dominant modifiable longevity factor. 3 SNPs combined.
supporting: rs3764814 (CETP): CT — ✓ CETP C allele — higher HDL cholesterol; associated with longevity in centenarian studies.
rs5882 (CETP): AG — ✓ CETP Val405Ile — associated with higher HDL and longevity.

adhd.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Adhd. GWAS polygenic score is +10.4 (above average); 2 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 141 genotyped. ADHD heritability ~70–80%; highly polygenic.

autism.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Autism. GWAS polygenic score is +8.2 (above average); 4 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 42 genotyped. Autism heritability ~80%; de novo variants play a major role.

bipolar_disorder.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Bipolar Disorder. GWAS polygenic score is +16.7 (above average); 7 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 190 genotyped. Bipolar disorder heritability ~70–80%; shares genetic overlap with schizophrenia.

schizophrenia.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Schizophrenia. GWAS polygenic score is +125.2 (above average); 29 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 965 genotyped. Schizophrenia heritability ~80%; major MHC/HLA component.

asthma.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Asthma. GWAS polygenic score is +40.4 (above average); 14 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 588 genotyped. Asthma heritability ~60–80%; strong gene-environment (allergen) interaction.

atrial_fibrillation.narrative: Low genetic signal for Atrial Fibrillation. GWAS polygenic score is +13.1 (above average); 1 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 141 genotyped. AF heritability ~20–30%; PITX2 locus is the strongest signal.

breast_cancer.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Breast Cancer. GWAS polygenic score is +80.9 (above average); 18 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 806 genotyped. BRCA1/2 are high-penetrance but rare; common variants each contribute modestly.

prostate_cancer.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Prostate Cancer. GWAS polygenic score is +61.2 (above average); 12 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 722 genotyped. Prostate cancer is ~57% heritable; 8q24 locus is the strongest common signal.

colorectal_cancer.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Colorectal Cancer. GWAS polygenic score is +55.1 (above average); 10 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 518 genotyped. CRC heritability ~35%; lifestyle (fibre, red meat, exercise) modifies genetic risk.

melanoma.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Melanoma. GWAS polygenic score is +14.1 (above average); 6 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 162 genotyped. Melanoma heritability ~50%; MC1R variants and UV exposure interact strongly. Skin protection is highly effective.

lung_cancer.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Lung Cancer. GWAS polygenic score is +31.6 (above average); 13 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 208 genotyped. Lung cancer genetic risk is dominated by smoking — genetic variants modify but do not replace smoking as the primary risk factor.

stroke.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Stroke. GWAS polygenic score is +31.4 (above average); 9 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 206 genotyped. Stroke heritability ~40%; many variants overlap with CAD and AF. Blood pressure control is the most effective intervention.

heart_failure.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Heart Failure. GWAS polygenic score is +61.4 (above average); 22 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 49 genotyped. Heart failure is largely downstream of CAD, hypertension, and diabetes — primary prevention of those conditions is key.

parkinson.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Parkinson. GWAS polygenic score is +27.9 (above average); 9 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 180 genotyped. Parkinson's heritability ~27%; LRRK2 and SNCA are major monogenic loci.

lupus.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Lupus. GWAS polygenic score is +49.4 (above average); 32 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 374 genotyped. Lupus heritability ~44%; strong HLA component.

rheumatoid_arthritis.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Rheumatoid Arthritis. GWAS polygenic score is +40.4 (above average); 10 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 757 genotyped. RA heritability ~60%; HLA-DRB1 accounts for ~30% of genetic variance.

inflammatory_bowel.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Inflammatory Bowel. GWAS polygenic score is +56.6 (above average); 18 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 851 genotyped. IBD heritability ~75% (Crohn's) / ~70% (UC); NOD2 is the strongest common risk gene.

psoriasis.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Psoriasis. GWAS polygenic score is +32.0 (above average); 13 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 310 genotyped. Psoriasis heritability ~60–70%; HLA-C*06:02 is the major risk allele.

crohn_disease.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Crohn Disease. GWAS polygenic score is +48.6 (above average); 13 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 584 genotyped. Crohn's heritability ~75%; NOD2 and ATG16L1 are key loci.

multiple_sclerosis.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Multiple Sclerosis. GWAS polygenic score is +28.1 (above average); 5 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 347 genotyped. MS heritability ~50%; HLA-DRB1*15:01 is the strongest risk allele.

gout.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Gout. GWAS polygenic score is +24.2 (above average); 8 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 195 genotyped. Gout heritability ~35–60%; SLC2A9 and ABCG2 are dominant uric acid loci. Dietary purine reduction and alcohol avoidance are effective interventions.

bladder_cancer.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Bladder Cancer. GWAS polygenic score is +13.0 (above average); 3 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 73 genotyped. Bladder cancer ~50% heritable for common variants; smoking is the strongest risk factor.

chronic_kidney_disease.narrative: Moderate genetic signal for Chronic Kidney Disease. GWAS polygenic score is +18.6 (above average); 7 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 95 genotyped. CKD heritability ~45%; blood pressure and diabetes control are primary interventions.

sleep_duration.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Sleep Duration. GWAS polygenic score is +7.8 (above average); 4 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 136 genotyped. Sleep duration heritability ~30–40%; circadian gene variants play a role.

vitamin_d.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Vitamin D Levels. GWAS polygenic score is +11.4 (above average); 4 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 71 genotyped. Vitamin D levels are ~50% heritable; GC and CYP2R1 are the major loci.

caffeine_metabolism.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Caffeine Metabolism. GWAS polygenic score is +5.5 (above average); 3 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 33 genotyped. Caffeine metabolism is ~50% heritable; CYP1A2 is the primary enzyme gene.

alcohol_consumption.narrative: Elevated genetic signal for Alcohol Consumption. GWAS polygenic score is +37.8 (above average); 10 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 78 genotyped. Alcohol metabolism heritability ~50%; ADH1B and ALDH2 are the dominant variants. ALDH2 variants (common in East Asians) cause alcohol flush reaction.

pharmacogenomics.narrative: Mild genetic signal for Pharmacogenomics. GWAS polygenic score is +6.4 (above average); 3 loci show elevated risk allele dosage out of 32 genotyped. Drug metabolism varies substantially by genotype; CYP2D6, CYP2C19, and TPMT are clinically actionable.
